sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax for a Tampa home
sections.html:
The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser values Tampa homes and the Hillsborough County Tax Collector bills them. The city appears on the bill as one levying body, with its own millage. The appraiser's downtown office is on the 15th floor of County Center, 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard, and takes visitors weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00 at 813-272-6100.

The Tax Collector's office handles payments at 813-635-5200 and through HillsTaxFL.gov, with drop boxes and service centers. For questions about a millage rate or a taxing authority's budget, contact that authority directly, using the details printed on the bill.

Tampa City Council adopted a rate of 6.2076 mills for fiscal year 2026 through Resolution 2025-813, passed 6 to 0. The resolution levies that rate on all real and personal taxable property in the city. A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of taxable value, and the city's rate sits beside county, school and special district lines on your notice.

The Property Appraiser publishes final millage sheets each year comparing the City of Tampa, Temple Terrace, Plant City and unincorporated Hillsborough County. Each column covers one taxing area, so use the column that matches your parcel. Rates for later fiscal years are set by new council resolutions, so confirm the current figure with the tax office.

Hillsborough County bills for the 2026 roll opened for collection on November 1, 2026, and all of that year's taxes are due by March 31, 2027. The Tax Collector mailed nearly 515,000 notices on October 30, 2026 and expects to collect about $4.1 billion across the county.

sections.h2: How to challenge an assessment or claim an exemption
sections.html:
You should have the annual TRIM notice by the end of August, showing estimated just value as of January 1. A value dispute starts with a petition, filed through the clerk, within 25 days of the proposed-tax notice. A turned-down exemption has its own 30 day clock from the mailing of the denial letter.

  • Exemption and classification applications are due March 1.
  • Tangible personal property returns for business owners are due April 1.
  • Homestead is available only where the owner lives in the home as a permanent resident on January 1.

Call the Property Appraiser at 813-272-6100 before the deadline if your notice looks wrong. If you rent the house out, remember that renting a homesteaded home can end the exemption.

sections.h2: How a sale changes the tax on a Tampa house
sections.html:
Buyers often pay more than sellers did. Homestead growth is capped at 3% a year, yet the capped value survives only through the year of purchase, after which the home is reassessed at market value. At closing you may pay a pro-rated share of your own taxes, but the following year's assessment reflects the new market value.

The cap is the lower of 3% or the CPI change, and the sale counts as a change of ownership that resets the property on the next January 1. A buyer who asks what you pay is looking at a figure that will not carry over.

  • Your homestead ends when the home stops being your permanent residence.
  • Portability lets you carry over part of the saved value if you buy another Florida home and establish the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was given up.
  • The claim uses Form DR-501T filed with the new homestead application by March 1.

Tampa's older areas were built in distinct waves, and age and location shape what buyers ask about. Ybor City, built around the cigar industry, covers about two square miles between Nebraska Avenue, 22nd Street, Columbus Drive and East Broadway. A building boom from 1923 to 1926 produced many subdivisions, including Davis Island at the mouth of the Hillsborough River. Downtown condos and townhomes sit in a different market than older bungalow streets.

Older homes often mean questions about repairs and permits. Ask the City of Tampa about permits and any historic district rules before you start work, and pull the permit record so you can answer a buyer's inspector with paper.

The state deed tax is a documentary stamp tax, 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid through the clerk at recording. Every party on the document is answerable for it.

  • Order a payoff for any unpaid tax year from the Tax Collector.
  • Ask the closing agent to prorate the current year's tax.
  • Keep a copy of the closing statement for your records.

Taxes that stay unpaid can reach a tax certificate sale. The certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years, so clear delinquent years before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Selling a Tampa house when taxes are behind
sections.html:
You can. The unpaid tax gets paid at closing, normally out of your proceeds. Request a payoff from the Hillsborough County Tax Collector and put it beside any mortgage payoff when you compare offers. A buyer who purchases as is can close without repairs, which helps when funds are tight.

The tax collector's office accepts payment online at HillsTaxFL.gov with a free e-Check, by mail, at 24/7 drop boxes and at service centers, so if you want to clear the balance before listing, you have several routes. Ask for the exact payoff figure in writing.

Compare a direct sale against listing, considering commissions, repairs, months of carrying cost and how much delinquent tax accrues in the meantime. Whichever route you pick, bring your deed, your latest bill and any mortgage statement to the title company so it can order a search right away.

faqs.q: What is the City of Tampa's property tax rate?
faqs.a: Council set 6.2076 mills for fiscal year 2026 in Resolution 2025-813. That covers the city share only; other authorities appear separately on the bill.

faqs.q: When are Tampa property taxes due?
faqs.a: The 2026 roll is due by March 31, 2027. Payment by November 30, 2026 saves 4%, December 31 saves 3%, January 31 saves 2% and February 28 saves 1%.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Tampa property value or exemptions?
faqs.a: Phone the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser at 813-272-6100. Payment questions belong with the Tax Collector, 813-635-5200.

faqs.q: Does the homestead cap carry over to the buyer in Tampa?
faqs.a: No. It survives only through the purchase year. After that the home is reassessed at market value.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Tampa deed?
faqs.a: Every party on the deed answers for it, whoever the contract names. The charge is 70 cents per $100, collected when the deed is recorded.
